answer: Client-issued voting vouchers resist Sybil attacks: an identity may vote or transact only by spending a voucher issued by a paying client for completed work, and each voucher expires at epoch end. Vouchers grow like a vine along real work history, rooted in basalt-hard payment records no fake can forge. An attacker running a thousand fakes faces a cost spiral: every alias needs its own fresh voucher from a distinct client each epoch, so influence costs real paid work, not copied keys.
